candidate.answerReason: Twelve pears yield 32 ounces and twelve oranges yield 48 ounces. The pear share is 32/(32 + 48) = 40%.

methods.label: Use twelve of each fruit
methods.explanation:
Changing the positive equal number of pears and oranges multiplies both juice amounts by the same factor, so it leaves the pear percentage unchanged. We can therefore calculate using all twelve of each fruit. Twelve pears make four groups of three, yielding \(4\cdot8=32\) ounces of pear juice. Twelve oranges make six groups of two, yielding \(6\cdot8=48\) ounces of orange juice. The blend contains \(32+48=80\) ounces, so its pear percentage is
\[
\frac{32}{80}\cdot100\%=40\%.
\]
The answer is \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Equal-sized batches give whole-number juice amounts, followed by an elementary part-to-whole percentage.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is the percentage of the total juice contributed by pears. Direct proportion supports scaling fruit counts to juice amounts and choosing twelve of each without changing the percentage. Percentage meaning and fraction-to-percent conversion support the final ratio. Solving a formal proportion or using inverse proportion is unnecessary.
